items.problem: `RoomMatchStartedEvent` of a match found in `None` is published while `MatchState` is still `None`, before `_enter_connecting`. open-game-works-core/skills/client-core/modules/realtime-core.md:271 defines the event as "when a non-host member became `Matching` or `Connecting`", while :186 publishes it before steps 3 to 5 of `join_match`. `ROOM_START` leaves the room `Open` (:184), so this is the path of every non-host member of a `start_room`. Run on the P2P transport in a temporary copy: a subscriber reads `match_state` 0 (`None`), and the `wait_match` it calls has already ended, because `wait_match` refuses `None` with a warn and `Failed` (realtime_core.gd:441). The match goes on to `Connecting` without that waiter. By reading, `leave` in the same subscriber only logs `leave: no match`, so the subscriber cannot leave the match with it. The publish line existed before the range

`_cancel_room_matching` ends a `join_match` that a `RoomChangedEvent` subscriber just started. `_leave_room_now` (:1166) and `_on_room_kicked` (:1182) check `MatchState` after they publish the event, so they treat that new `Matching` as the `Matching` of the room that was left. Run on the fake transport in a temporary copy: a member in `None` and a subscriber that calls `join_match` on `Left` or `Kicked`. The state is `None` and the `join_match` has ended where `Matching` and a waiting call are expected, and on `Kicked` the `start_matching` count is 0. By reading, its `status` is `Cancelled`. open-game-works-core/skills/client-core/modules/realtime-core.md:177 and :178 cancel the `Matching` of the room and do not set this order. The check existed before the range
